findings.description: The slots service defines IFromUser.id as number, but the copied SlotInfo type changes it to string. Preserve id: number in the local response type.
findings.failureMode: The unchanged calendar-view hook call fails TypeScript checking because fromUser.id in the migrated response type is string rather than number.
findings.title: Keep out-of-office fromUser IDs numeric

findings.description: The schedules list returns numeric weekday indexes, and ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper passes each result to getScheduleListItemData, whose availability.days contract is number[]. Declaring days as string[] makes that existing call fail TypeScript checking. Preserve number[] in the local response type.
findings.failureMode: Building/type-checking the schedules list fails because the new hook result with availability.days: string[] is not assignable to the transformer's number[] contract.
findings.title: Use numeric availability weekdays

findings.description: The migrated Slot type changes userIds from number[] to string[], while the server still produces numeric IDs and onTimeslotsLoaded still forwards its data without conversion. Existing callbacks typed for numeric IDs, or callbacks using slot.userIds?.includes(42), now fail TypeScript checking. Preserve userIds?: number[] in the moved type.
findings.failureMode: A previously valid onTimeslotsLoaded callback with numeric userIds is no longer assignable; consuming IDs as numbers now fails type checking.
findings.title: Keep slot user IDs numeric

The source booker directory is excluded from the tarball, so consumers importing types from @calcom/atoms/booker/types get a module-not-found error after publishing. findings.title: Export booker types from a packaged path

findings.description: Only name is checked before this cast. For example, validateCreateScheduleInput({ name: "work", eventTypeId: "oops", schedule: [[{ start: "bad", end: null }]] }) succeeds, although the returned type requires a numeric eventTypeId and Date boundaries. findings.title: Validate all fields before returning CreateScheduleInput

findings.description: The new error-level @calcom/trpc/** ban also matches the remaining QueryCell imports in ConferencingAppsViewPlatformWrapper.tsx and SelectedCalendarsSettingsPlatformWrapper.tsx. findings.title: Migrate QueryCell imports with the new ban

findings.description: validateCreateScheduleInput(null) throws a plain Error whose code is undefined. The repository mandate requires categorized errors, so callers cannot identify this invalid-payload failure by its typed code. Use ErrorWithCode with ErrorCode.RequestBodyInvalid and input context here.
findings.failureMode: A malformed top-level input yields an uncategorized Error (code is undefined) rather than the required typed validation error.
findings.title: Categorize invalid-object validation errors

findings.description: validateCreateScheduleInput({}) throws a plain Error whose code is undefined. This separately violates the required categorized-error contract for bad names, so callers cannot identify the field-validation failure by its typed code. Use ErrorWithCode with ErrorCode.RequestBodyInvalid and name-field context here.
findings.failureMode: A missing, empty, or non-string name yields an uncategorized Error (code is undefined) rather than the required typed validation error.
findings.title: Categorize invalid-name validation errors

findings.description: The new helper uses single-quoted literals at lines 39–40 and 45–46, while the mandated Biome configuration sets quoteStyle to double. Running biome format on this file exits nonzero with a formatting error. Format the helper using the repository configuration.
findings.failureMode: The new file fails the standardized Biome formatting check due to the helper's quote style.
findings.title: Format the new validation helper with Biome

findings.description: A path cannot have both extensions, so `&&` disables validation for all JSON/JSON5 configs. Serde does not enforce the schema's `productName` path-character restriction: `productName: "/tmp/existing"` now loads successfully. On macOS, bundling then targets `/tmp/existing.app` and recursively deletes that directory if it exists, outside the build output. Restore `||` so these inputs are rejected before bundling.
findings.failureMode: A JSON/JSON5 config with an absolute or traversal-containing productName bypasses its schema restriction and causes macOS bundle cleanup to delete an existing directory outside the output tree.
findings.title: Use OR so JSON schema validation still runs

findings.description: Valid configs store the identifier in the top-level `identifier` string; `bundle` is an object or absent, so this lookup records `None`. Mobile `write_options` then returns `app configuration is missing an identifier`, aborting Android/iOS dev and build commands. The Android Studio/Xcode scripts also panic in `read_options` on that missing value. Restore the `identifier` lookup.
findings.failureMode: An ordinary mobile app with a valid identifier cannot start its CLI option server, and direct Android Studio/Xcode script invocations panic when read_options sees None.
findings.title: Read the original top-level identifier

findings.description: The merged `value` is discarded instead of assigned to `config_metadata.inner`. With a loaded `build.devUrl` on port 8000, merging a port-9000 override returns success and sets `TAURI_CONFIG` to 9000, while the returned handle still contains 8000. Restore the deleted `config_metadata.inner = serde_json::from_value(value).context("failed to parse config")?;` assignment; extension metadata does not update the effective config.
findings.failureMode: A nonempty merge_with override leaves the returned configuration stale and inconsistent with TAURI_CONFIG, as reproduced with two different dev URLs.
findings.title: Write the merged value back to the cached config

findings.description: With tab swiping enabled, the right skeleton starts at the container's trailing edge and is container width minus 32 points wide. This removes the `productName` pattern guard: an absolute name such as `/tmp/existing` now deserializes and reaches the macOS bundler, which joins `${productName}.app` to its output directory and calls `remove_dir_all` if it exists. It can therefore delete `/tmp/existing.app` outside the build directory. Restore `||` to validate both formats.
findings.failureMode: Schema-invalid path-valued productName is accepted, escapes the output directory and causes the macOS bundler to delete an existing external .app directory.
findings.title: Restore the schema-validation format alternatives

Mobile `write_options` then fails with `app configuration is missing an identifier`, breaking Android/iOS dev and build; the IDE scripts also call `read_options`, whose `.expect("failed to read CLI options")` panics on the same error. Read `identifier` as before.
findings.failureMode: Every valid config loses its original identifier; mobile option exchange errors and Android Studio/Xcode scripts panic.
findings.title: Restore the top-level identifier lookup

Restore the deserialization/assignment as well as recording the extension.
findings.failureMode: merge_with returns success but the loaded configuration is unchanged after a nonempty patch.
findings.title: Store the merged config back in the handle

findings.description: Choosing Stays in / Not Ready with threshold 1 still writes the status to expect and leaves after empty. The not-ready transition then satisfies the expected-event count, so proactive evaluation discards its bucket and never alerts when the pool remains Not Ready beyond the window. work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:36 has the same defect. In Proactive mode, store the entry status in after and expect exit-status events instead.
findings.failureMode: Proactive status forms monitor the absence of a transition instead of time spent in that status
findings.title: Bind stays-in statuses to the starting event

findings.description: Clearing the expected-events textarea stores [""] because split("\n") always returns at least one entry. The schema accepts this, but the backend treats only an actually empty expect set as 'any event'; [""] matches no nonempty event. Thus two visually empty forms behave differently, and a cleared Reactive trigger silently stops firing. Handle an empty textarea as [] instead of testing the split array's length.
findings.failureMode: Clearing custom expected events creates a nonmatching empty-string event filter
findings.title: Preserve the empty filter when clearing custom events

findings.description: The new Within input and EventTriggerSchema both accept a five-second Proactive window as valid, but the backend's EventTrigger validator rejects every nonzero window below 10 seconds. This produces an unusable trigger configuration instead of validation feedback. The same min={0} appears in custom-trigger-fields.tsx:80, work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx:98, and work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:98. Require at least 10 seconds in these Proactive inputs and their form validation.
findings.failureMode: New proactive forms produce event triggers rejected by backend validation for within 1-9 seconds
findings.title: Enforce the backend minimum for proactive windows

findings.description: The work-pool threshold uses parseInt while the other numeric inputs use Number. A valid number-input value such as 1e2 is parsed as 1 instead of 100, so the automation fires at the wrong threshold. Convert the full numeric value and validate that it is an integer.
findings.failureMode: Exponent-form threshold input silently creates a different threshold
findings.title: Parse the full numeric threshold value

findings.description: The new global parseInt call violates the configured error-level useNumberNamespace rule. `biome ci` reports this changed line and exits nonzero, failing the UI v2 Checks lint job. Use a compliant Number conversion rather than the global function.
findings.failureMode: Required Biome CI check fails on the global parseInt call
findings.title: Avoid the global parseInt rejected by Biome

Every successful HINCRBYFLOAT is rejected on replicas and during AOF replay: an acknowledged 1-to-2.1 increment reloads as 1. With propagation-error-behavior=panic, the malformed command crashes the replica. Pass 7 so the final value is included.
findings.failureMode: Every successful HINCRBYFLOAT emits a malformed HSETEX command, losing the increment in replication/AOF and crashing when propagation errors are configured to panic.
findings.title: Include all seven objects in the rewritten command

findings.description: The old call used `HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL`; dropping HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL makes hashTypeSet clear expiration on the primary in both hash encodings. After HSETEX h1 EX 100 FIELDS 1 f1 1 and HINCRBYFLOAT h1 f1 1.1, HTTL returns -1 and the field no longer expires. Restore HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL here; the rewritten command's KEEPTTL only affects replicas/AOF.
findings.failureMode: An increment of a non-expired hash field with a TTL clears the TTL on the primary.
findings.title: Preserve the field TTL on the primary

findings.description: Removing static from addHashFieldToReply gives this file-local helper external linkage (a non-LTO object exports _addHashFieldToReply). All callers remain in t_hash.c and there is no public declaration. This violates mandatory repository rule 7 and exposes an internal implementation symbol. Restore static on this definition.

findings.title: Keep the file-local reply helper static

Defining a registered TemplateTransformNode subclass for version 2 and requesting '2' or 'latest' now produces a version-1 TemplateTransformNode and its output, whereas the base factory instantiated the mapped class. With the sandbox unavailable, the node fails even though the injected renderer could return the output. Use an explicit None check at both sites.

findings.description: The removed keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8') conversion was needed for inputs/outputs stored by json.dumps with ensure_ascii=True. A run containing 中文 is stored as \u4e2d\u6587, so the new raw-character pattern returns no matching logs. JSON-encode the keyword before LIKE escaping for the inputs/outputs predicates; retain a separate raw-keyword pattern for EndUser.session_id.
findings.failureMode: Workflow log keyword search no longer finds inputs/outputs stored with JSON Unicode escapes after removing encoding of the search keyword.
findings.title: Preserve JSON encoding in workflow log search

findings.description: ClickZetta connections are configured with cz.sql.string.literal.escape.mode='quote', where backslashes remain literal. This f-string emits two backslashes inside the SQL ESCAPE literal, but LIKE requires a single constant character. When full-text search falls back to _search_by_like, even an ordinary keyword now produces invalid SQL. Emit a one-backslash SQL literal for the configured quote mode.
findings.failureMode: ClickZetta LIKE fallback fails SQL validation because its ESCAPE string contains two characters under the configured quote-only string escaping mode.
findings.title: Emit one ClickZetta escape character in quote mode

findings.description: With IRIS_TEXT_INDEX=False, searching test_data now binds %test\_data%, but ESCAPE '|' makes the backslash literal and the underscore a wildcard. A document containing test_data is therefore omitted; percent and backslash queries are affected too. Declare backslash as the escape character, matching escape_like_pattern.
findings.failureMode: IRIS LIKE fallback returns missing or incorrect documents for literal percent/underscore/backslash queries because the parameter and SQL use different escape characters.
findings.title: Match the IRIS ESCAPE clause to the helper

findings.description: On MySQL configured with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES (e.g. DB_EXTRAS=sql_mode=NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES), LIKE has no default escape character. This branch now passes %test\_data% for not contains test_data, incorrectly retaining documents whose metadata contains test_data. Pass escape="\\" to notlike, as the positive string-filter branches do.
findings.failureMode: Negative metadata string filters evaluate escaped wildcard/backslash values incorrectly on supported MySQL connections with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES.
findings.title: Declare ESCAPE for negative metadata matches

findings.description: rewriteClientCommandVector copies exactly argc objects, so 6 drops newobj and propagates HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field without its value. Replicas and AOF replay reject this command. With appendonly enabled, HSET h f 1 followed by HINCRBYFLOAT h f 1.1 returns the incremented value, but restarting restores 1, losing the acknowledged increment. Use an argument count of 7.
findings.failureMode: Any successful HINCRBYFLOAT writes a truncated HSETEX command to replication/AOF, losing increments on replicas and on persistence replay.
findings.title: Pass seven arguments to the HSETEX rewrite

findings.description: Removing HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL from the local hashTypeSet makes HINCRBYFLOAT persist an unexpired field on the primary. HSETEX h1 EX 100 FIELDS 1 f1 1 followed by HINCRBYFLOAT h1 f1 1.1 changes HTTL to -1 instead of preserving the deadline, in both hash encodings. Restore HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL for the local update; replay's KEEPTTL cannot restore the primary's TTL.
findings.failureMode: HINCRBYFLOAT on a field with an unexpired TTL changes its TTL to persistent on the primary.
findings.title: Preserve the field TTL on the primary

findings.description: Removing static exports addHashFieldToReply even though all callers remain in t_hash.c and no public declaration is added. This introduces an unnecessary global symbol and violates mandatory AGENTS.md rule 7 for file-local helpers. Restore static on this definition.

findings.description: Normal reader-mode taps dispatch .showReaderMode, but this value routes them to toggleReaderModeLongPressAction(), which saves the page to ReadingList.db instead of toggling reader view. This also persists a private tab's URL and title without a save request. For an existing marked-as-read entry, the INSERT OR REPLACE resets its read status. findings.description: For an active reader page in non-private mode, the changed default branch now passes isEnabled=true instead of false. ToolbarTelemetry currently puts that argument into the isPrivate extra, so this newly records is_private=true. findings.description: For an active reader-mode tab, this predicate now forwards http://localhost:…/reader-mode/page?url=… as the cancel-edit URL. A DOM/React probe confirms raw input='1e2' yields threshold=1, unlike the other forms' Number conversion. Use Number(e.target.value) so the trigger form does not silently change the requested count.

Entering 5 seconds passes EventTriggerSchema validation and lets the wizard advance, but the backend EventTrigger validator rejects it because proactive intervals must be at least 10 seconds. Enforce that minimum in form validation and the inputs.

Add integer validation for these thresholds instead of accepting an invalid trigger.
findings.failureMode: A user can enter threshold=1.5, advance past the trigger step, and submit a payload with a noninteger event count despite the backend requiring an int.
findings.title: Reject fractional event thresholds

findings.description: SelectLightTheme taps lightThemeView, and ThemeSelectionView makes the options mutually exclusive. The new darkThemeView query therefore returns "0" after a successful Light selection, so the following assertion fails on a correct app and FullFunctionalTestPlan reports a failure. Restore this query to lightThemeView.

findings.title: Read the light-theme button after selecting Light

findings.description: Moving `navigator.goto(NewTabScreen)` after the Done tap leaves the UI on TopSitesSettingsViewController when Done is queried. That controller has no Done button (only the Homepage and main Settings controllers install it), so testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection now times out before the new goto runs. Restore navigation before the Done tap so the stack is popped to a controller that provides Done.
findings.failureMode: The test opens Shortcuts and disables its switch, then waits for a Done button that does not exist on that screen because the navigation that previously returned to Settings was moved after the tap.
findings.title: Return from Shortcuts before tapping Done

findings.description: WorkflowRun inputs/outputs are stored with `json.dumps` (ASCII escaping enabled). Replacing the former `encode('unicode_escape')...replace(r'\u', r'\\u')` with escaping the raw keyword means a search such as `你好` no longer matches the stored `\u4f60\u597d`, so existing runs disappear from search results. Encode the keyword to its stored JSON representation before LIKE escaping for these two fields, keeping the raw keyword for EndUser.session_id.
findings.failureMode: Console/API workflow-log keyword search for non-ASCII input/output content returns no matching runs because it compares raw Unicode against ASCII-escaped JSON text.
findings.title: Preserve JSON encoding when searching workflow inputs and outputs

findings.description: The connection setup selects `cz.sql.string.literal.escape.mode = 'quote'`, which does not backslash-unescape string literals. This f-string emits `ESCAPE '\\'` (two actual backslashes), not a one-character escape, so the LIKE fallback fails for even a normal query when full-text search fails. Emit a single backslash in the SQL escape literal under the configured quote mode.
findings.failureMode: A configured ClickZetta connection running the full-text LIKE fallback receives an invalid multi-character ESCAPE expression and fails instead of returning documents.
findings.title: Use a one-character ESCAPE literal in ClickZetta quote mode

findings.description: With IRIS_TEXT_INDEX disabled, the helper emits backslash escapes but the SQL declares `ESCAPE '|'`. A search for `50%` or `test_data` therefore requires an extra backslash and misses the literal document text; pipe characters in otherwise normal queries are consumed as escapes too. Use backslash as the SQL escape character to match the generated pattern.
findings.failureMode: IRIS fallback literal searches miss matching documents because the SQL escape character is not the character inserted in the bound pattern.
findings.title: Match the IRIS ESCAPE character to the helper

findings.description: Unlike the other three string predicates, `not contains` passes the escaped value to NOT LIKE without `escape='\\'`. On a supported MySQL database with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES enabled, backslash is not the default LIKE escape: `not contains '50%'` then keeps documents whose metadata is `50% discount`, because it searches for a literal backslash instead of excluding the percent text. Pass the same explicit escape argument as the positive predicates.
findings.failureMode: Metadata NOT-CONTAINS filters include documents they are supposed to exclude on MySQL configurations that disable the default backslash escape.
findings.title: Declare the escape character for NOT LIKE as well

findings.description: A normal reader-mode tap dispatches showReaderMode, but this reducer now returns readerModeLongPressAction. BrowserViewController handles that by calling createRecordWithURL on the reading list, not enableReaderMode/disableReaderMode, so tapping the icon saves the page (or reports that it already exists) and never opens/closes the reader. Restore displayView: .readerMode; this also fixes the summarizer long-press and menu callers that dispatch showReaderMode.
findings.failureMode: On a readable page, a reader-mode tap adds the page to the reading list or produces an already-exists error, without opening/closing reader mode.
findings.title: Keep reader-mode taps on the reader-mode display action

findings.description: For an .active reader in a normal tab, the new default supplies true for isEnabled instead of false. ToolbarTelemetry currently maps this argument into the Glean is_private extra, so these taps now incorrectly record is_private=true; a private .available reader is instead recorded as non-private. The existing reader-mode middleware test also receives true where it asserts false. Restore the post-tap mapping (.available: true, default: false).
findings.failureMode: Reversing the reader-mode transition boolean corrupts previously-correct is_private extras for active normal readers and available private readers, and fails the existing middleware test.
findings.title: Restore the reader-mode telemetry transition

findings.description: With an active reader tab, selectedTab.url is the internal http://localhost:<port>/reader-mode/page?... URL. This condition now passes it into cancelEdit, whose reducer overrides the decoded article URL in AddressBarState. The location view does not decode it, so Cancel/Menu/Tabs displays localhost and subsequent editing exposes the internal reader URL. Restore the reader-mode exclusion so the nil action URL preserves the display URL already in state.
findings.failureMode: Opening Cancel/Menu/Tabs while viewing a reader-mode page changes the address bar from the article's decoded URL to the internal localhost reader URL.
findings.title: Do not replace the display URL with the reader's internal URL

findings.description: Removing private makes this implementation-only dependency readable throughout Client, including its collection-control methods such as setUpload. AGENTS.md rule 11 explicitly requires private access for implementation details. All existing consumers inject through init rather than reading this property; retain private let so access outside ToolbarTelemetry is still rejected.
findings.failureMode: The required compile-time access boundary is lost: other Client code can now read ToolbarTelemetry.gleanWrapper and invoke dependency methods directly, contrary to the mandatory access-control contract.
findings.title: Keep the telemetry dependency private

findings.description: `start:prod` runs CommonJS output with plain Node, but this import targets a raw `.ts` module in `@calcom/features`. Nest leaves the package import unchanged, and Node 20 cannot resolve this extensionless subpath, so loading the newly wired controller aborts API startup with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Import `TeamService` from the existing built `@calcom/platform-libraries` export; this also fixes the restricted-import lint error.
findings.failureMode: Production API startup loads TeamsInviteController and tries to require @calcom/features/ee/teams/services/teamService, an extensionless source path with no JavaScript runtime entrypoint; Node throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND.
findings.title: Import the built TeamService from platform-libraries

findings.description: The new invite endpoint is guarded with `TEAM_MEMBER`, so an authenticated regular member can create and share team invitation links even though invitation creation is admin-only. `TeamService.createInvite` has no user or admin check. Use `TEAM_ADMIN` so the guard rejects non-admin members before generating an invite.
findings.failureMode: A regular team member can POST to /v2/teams/:teamId/invite and receive a usable invite link despite lacking invitation-administration permission.
findings.title: Require team admin permission to create invites

findings.description: A new invite returns the constant `invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}` identifier instead of the random value stored in `VerificationToken.token`. Repeated requests return the same `data.token`, it differs from the token in `inviteLink`, and using it to retrieve or redeem the invitation fails with not-found. Return `newToken.token` or the generated `token`.
findings.failureMode: A new invite returns a constant identifier as data.token, so token-based redemption fails and new invite token assertions fail.
findings.title: Return the invite token, not its identifier

findings.description: For a regular team (`parentId = null`, `isOrganization = false`), this inverted condition now returns `/signup?token=...`. Signup redirects logged-in invitees to `/` without consuming the token; for logged-out invitees it disables the email field after prepopulating it with the non-email identifier `invite-link-for-teamId-...`. Both paths fail to join the team. Restore `if (!isOrgContext)` so regular teams use `/teams` and organization contexts use signup/onboarding.
findings.failureMode: Regular-team invitees receive a signup URL that either drops the invitation for existing logged-in users or supplies an invalid disabled email for new users.
findings.title: Keep regular-team invites on the teams route

findings.description: The new response schema promises that every `inviteLink` opens signup, but an organization-subteam request returns `/teams?token=...`, so the generated Swagger description contradicts a supported response. Correct the description to cover both context-dependent destinations; restoring the service's original routing alone still leaves the description wrong for regular teams.
findings.failureMode: The new API response documentation claims the signup/onboarding route for returned /teams links, so the generated contract is wrong for a supported team context.
findings.title: Document both invite link destinations

findings.description: The helper now returns `FileWriteError`, but `prepare_tools` returns `crate::Result<PathBuf>` and propagates this result with `?` at five call sites. No `From<FileWriteError>` exists for `crate::Error`; its `From<anyhow::Error>` does not chain automatically. Linux bundler/CLI builds therefore fail with E0277. Map the new helper error into `crate::Error` before propagating it.
findings.failureMode: Linux tauri-bundler/tauri-cli builds cannot compile because From<FileWriteError> is absent for crate::Error.
findings.title: Convert helper errors into the bundler error type

findings.description: Each download/cache-miss branch calls this helper on a file that does not exist. Moving `set_permissions` ahead of `fs::write` makes it return NotFound before creating any file, so a fresh AppImage tools cache fails on AppRun and a partially populated cache fails on each missing tool or GStreamer script. Create/write the file first, then chmod it.
findings.failureMode: Missing AppRun/linuxdeploy/GStreamer/AppImage plugin paths cannot be created because chmod runs before fs::write.
findings.title: Write the tool file before setting its permissions

findings.description: When the cached GTK script is missing, `gtk.exists()` is false and the embedded script is never installed. With the other tools already cached, `prepare_tools` succeeds but `bundle_project` always passes `--plugin gtk`, so linuxdeploy fails to find the plugin and no AppImage is produced. Restore `!gtk.exists()` to populate missing scripts.
findings.failureMode: A tools cache without linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh is never populated; when other tools are cached the required linuxdeploy --plugin gtk invocation fails.
findings.title: Install the GTK plugin on cache misses

findings.description: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` reports this new statement and exits nonzero, requiring the `.map_err(...)` call on a continuation line. This fails mandatory formatting rule 3 and the repository's rustfmt CI job. Run rustfmt on the changed Rust file.
findings.failureMode: The required cargo fmt --all -- --check job fails on the newly added permission update statement.
findings.title: Format the permission update with rustfmt

findings.description: The vendored script is copied from linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk, whose pre-existing MIT license requires including `Copyright 2018-2019 TheAssassin and the linuxdeploy contributors` and its permission notice with copies. Neither this file nor the packaged licenses contains that attribution. Publishing the crate now redistributes the entire script (also embedded via `include_bytes!`) without its required notice. Add the upstream MIT notice to the vendored script so source and embedded copies retain it.
findings.failureMode: Publishing tauri-bundler or its CLI binary redistributes an upstream MIT-licensed script without the required copyright attribution and permission notice.
findings.title: Preserve the GTK plugin's MIT attribution

findings.description: The new `FileWriteError` enum derives only `Debug` and implements `Display`/`Error` by hand. Repository compliance rule 8 explicitly requires custom error enums to derive `thiserror::Error` with `#[error(...)]` variants and rejects manual trait implementations, so this new type fails the required structured-error compliance. Use the existing thiserror dependency for this enum.
findings.failureMode: The new custom error fails the mandatory structured-error compliance rule because Display/Error are implemented manually.
findings.title: Derive the new error with thiserror

findings.description: The new local availability response declares days as string[], whereas the existing schedule transformer accepts number[]. ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper passes useAtomGetAllSchedules().data.schedules directly to getScheduleListItemData, so this change makes that call fail TypeScript checking. Preserve days: number[] to match the handler/Prisma response.
findings.failureMode: Type-check/build rejects getScheduleListItemData(schedule) in ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper because availability.days is string[] instead of number[].
findings.title: Keep availability days as numeric weekday indexes

findings.description: The server's IFromUser.id is number, but the copied SlotInfo declares string. EventTypeCalendarViewComponent passes useAvailableSlots().data to useAvailableTimeSlots, whose schedule parameter still expects IGetAvailableSlots with a numeric fromUser.id. This makes that unchanged call fail TypeScript checking, even when no out-of-office slot is returned. Change this field to number to preserve the response contract.
findings.failureMode: Atoms type-check/build fails on useAvailableTimeSlots({ schedule: schedule.data, eventDuration }) because copied SlotInfo.fromUser.id is string, not the expected number.
findings.title: Keep fromUser.id numeric in the copied slot response
